course.title: Java Programming
course.subtitle: From Absolute Beginner to Advanced Java Developer
course.tagline: Zero se professional Java — JDK 21, real compiler, 20 modules aur interview-ready practice
course.description: BroCode ka complete Java Mastery course: 20 modules from your first class to virtual threads, JDBC and Spring Boot thinking. Hinglish explanations, real JDK 21 compilation in Code Bro, 100+ coding questions, 80+ interview answers, 50 debugging challenges, 30 labs, 15 projects aur module-wise assessments.
prerequisites: Programming ka koi experience zaroori nahi — Python ya C helpful hai, mandatory nahi
outcomes: Java program likhna, javac se compile karna aur JVM par chalana
OOP, collections, generics aur exception handling ko confidently use karna
Lambdas, Streams aur multithreading se real data process karna
JDBC aur Spring Boot ke concepts se backend development start karna
Debugging, testing aur design patterns se production-quality code likhna
Java developer interviews ke core aur advanced questions ka structured answer dena

modules.title: Java Introduction
modules.goal: Java kya hai, kaise chalta hai, aur apna pehla program compile karke chalana.
modules.brief: A program is a list of instructions: take input, store values, calculate, print a result. In Java those instructions live inside a class, and execution starts at a method with the exact signature public static void main(String[] args).

modules.title: Java Fundamentals
modules.goal: Variables, primitive types, operators, input/output aur type conversion ko confidently use karna.
modules.brief: A variable is a named box with a fixed type. int holds whole numbers, double holds decimals, boolean holds true/false, char holds one character. The type decides how much memory the box takes and which operations are legal.

modules.title: Strings
modules.goal: String immutability, pool, comparison aur StringBuilder ko theek se samajhna.
modules.brief: A String is immutable: once created, its characters never change. Calling toUpperCase() returns a new String; the original is untouched. That sounds wasteful, but immutability makes strings safe to share, cache and use as HashMap keys.

modules.title: Conditional Statements
modules.goal: if, else-if, switch aur modern switch expressions se decisions lena.
modules.brief: An if statement evaluates a boolean and runs its block only when that boolean is true. else runs when it is false, and else-if chains let you test conditions in order — the first true branch wins, and the rest are skipped.

modules.title: Loops
modules.goal: for, while, do-while, nested loops aur break/continue par command.
modules.brief: Use for when you know how many times to repeat or you are walking an index range. Use while when the repetition depends on something that changes inside the loop, such as reading until input ends. Use do-while when the body must run at least once, like showing a menu before checking whether the user wants to quit.

modules.title: Number Logic and Recursion
modules.goal: Prime, palindrome, fibonacci jaise number problems aur recursion ka call stack.
modules.brief: Most number problems are digit arithmetic: n % 10 gives the last digit, n / 10 removes it. Repeating that pair lets you sum digits, reverse a number, or check a palindrome without converting to text.

modules.title: Methods
modules.goal: Methods likhna, parameters pass karna, return values aur overloading samajhna.
modules.brief: Methods turn a long main into named steps. A method signature is the name plus the parameter types; that is what the compiler uses to pick the right method. The return type is not part of the signature, which is why two methods cannot differ only by return type.

modules.title: Arrays
modules.goal: Arrays declare, traverse, search, sort aur 2D arrays handle karna.
modules.brief: Arrays give you numbered slots. int[] marks = new int[5] creates five ints initialised to 0; the valid indexes are 0 to 4. Asking for marks[5] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, because the last valid index is always length - 1.

modules.title: Object-Oriented Programming
modules.goal: Class, object, constructor, encapsulation aur object lifecycle par solid foundation.
modules.brief: A class groups the data and the operations that belong together. Each object gets its own copy of the instance fields; methods describe what every instance can do. Creating an object with new runs a constructor, which is where required state is set up.

modules.title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
modules.goal: extends, super, method overriding aur runtime polymorphism ka asli behaviour.
modules.brief: A subclass inherits accessible fields and methods and can add its own. super(...) calls the parent constructor and must be the first statement; super.method() calls the parent's version. Constructors are not inherited.

modules.title: Abstraction and Interfaces
modules.goal: Abstract classes, interfaces, default methods aur SOLID ka practical use.
modules.brief: An abstract class is a partially built class: it can have fields, constructors and concrete methods, plus abstract methods that subclasses must implement. It expresses a shared identity with shared code. You extend one.

modules.title: Packages and Advanced Java Syntax
modules.goal: Packages, enums, records, sealed types, annotations aur generics ka first look.
modules.brief: Packages prevent name collisions and express ownership: com.brocode.shop.model, com.brocode.shop.service. The package statement must match the directory path, and import brings a type into scope without copying it.

modules.title: Exception Handling
modules.goal: Checked/unchecked exceptions, try/catch/finally aur custom exceptions ko theek se use karna.
modules.brief: When a method cannot complete normally it throws an exception. The JVM unwinds the stack looking for a matching catch. If none is found, the thread terminates and prints a stack trace. Catching lets you recover, translate or add context.

modules.title: Collection Framework
modules.goal: List, Set, Map, Queue aur unke trade-offs ko complexity ke saath samajhna.
modules.brief: Choose by the question you are answering. Need order and duplicates? List (ArrayList for fast indexing, LinkedList for frequent ends). Need uniqueness? Set (HashSet for speed, LinkedHashSet for insertion order, TreeSet for sorted order). Need lookup by key? Map.

modules.title: Generics and Wrapper Classes
modules.goal: Type-safe generic code, bounds, wildcards aur autoboxing ke traps.
modules.brief: Before generics, a List held Object and every read needed a cast that could fail at runtime. With List<String>, the compiler rejects adding an Integer and read results need no cast. The type parameter is a promise the compiler verifies.

modules.title: File Handling and Java I/O
modules.goal: Files, streams, readers/writers, NIO aur try-with-resources se safe I/O.
modules.brief: A Path locates a file; Files performs operations on it. Files.readString/readAllLines load text, Files.writeString/write create or overwrite, and Files.lines streams a large file line by line without loading it all into memory.

modules.title: Functional Java
modules.goal: Lambdas, functional interfaces, Streams aur Optional se data pipelines banana.
modules.brief: A functional interface has one abstract method, so the compiler can infer the lambda's shape: Predicate<T> is T → boolean, Function<T,R> is T → R, Consumer<T> is T → void, Supplier<T> is () → T. Method references (String::length) are shorthand when an existing method already fits.

modules.title: Multithreading and Concurrency
modules.goal: Threads, race conditions, synchronization, executors aur CompletableFuture.
modules.brief: Every Java program starts with the main thread. You create another by implementing Runnable and passing it to a Thread, but production code submits tasks to an ExecutorService so threads are pooled and reused instead of created per request.

modules.title: Database and Backend Development
modules.goal: JDBC, SQL integration, Maven/Gradle, REST concepts aur Spring Boot ka mental model.
modules.brief: JDBC follows a fixed flow: load a driver (automatic since JDBC 4), open a Connection, prepare a statement, execute, read the ResultSet, close everything. A PreparedStatement sends SQL and values separately, so user input can never change the query structure — that is the defence against SQL injection.

modules.title: Professional Java and Career Preparation
modules.goal: JVM internals, design patterns, clean code, testing aur interview readiness.
modules.brief: The JVM stores each thread's call frames on its stack and objects on the heap. The garbage collector reclaims objects that are no longer reachable; you influence it by allocating less and releasing references, not by calling System.gc(). Class loading happens once per class loader: load, link, initialise.
